The intervention is physical radiation delivery, so 'target engagement' means the radiation was delivered to the intended anatomical site. Given this is a completed trial with reported outcomes, we can assume the radiation was delivered as planned, though no biomarker data confirms cellular DNA damage. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The proposed mechanism is high-dose focused radiation causing DNA damage and cell death in residual tumor cells. No biomarker data is available to confirm DNA damage or apoptosis markers, so we cannot directly assess pathway modulation. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint (Local Control at 1 year) was met. Overall, 13/39 patients (33.3%) achieved local control, with 23/39 (59%) achieving no evidence of disease. This represents clinical benefit in the target population. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: The trial shows clear population heterogeneity - patients achieving NED had much better outcomes (23 patients) compared to those with progression (2 patients) or relapse (1 patient). This suggests the intervention works well in a subset of patients. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This is a single-arm trial with no control group, which limits interpretation. However, the 59% rate of no evidence of disease appears clinically meaningful for post-surgical brain metastases. The trial was adequately powered and completed as planned.
